content: A unicornuate uterus results from the failure of one Müllerian duct to elongate properly, while the other duct develops normally. This condition accounts for approximately 20% of all Müllerian duct anomalies. The embryological tendency for the unicornuate uterus to predominantly occur on the right side remains unexplained. Women with a unicornuate uterus experience spontaneous abortion rates ranging from 41% to 62%. Premature birth rates in these patients are reported to range between 10% and 20%. Fetal survival rates vary from 38% to 57%, with pooled data suggesting an average survival rate of approximately 40%. Renal abnormalities are more frequently associated with a unicornuate uterus compared to other types of Müllerian duct anomalies. These renal anomalies are reported in 40% of patients with a unicornuate uterus and are always located on the same side as the rudimentary uterine horn. Renal agenesis, or the complete absence of a kidney, is the most commonly reported renal abnormality, occurring in 67% of cases. Diagnosis Hysterosalpingography (HSG) On HSG imaging, the endometrial cavity of a unicornuate uterus typically appears fusiform in shape, tapering at the apex and draining into a single fallopian tube. The uterus is often displaced from the midline. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) MRI findings of a unicornuate uterus include a curved and elongated uterine structure, with the external contour resembling the shape of a banana. The uterine volume is reduced, and the configuration is asymmetrical. Despite these abnormalities, the normal zonal anatomy of the myometrium is preserved.
